properties.description: Identifies unusually large NRD ingest volume that may indicate bulk registration campaigns.
properties.displayName: WhoisFreaks - burst of newly registered domains
properties.query:
union WhoisFreaksNRD_CL, WhoisFreaksNRDNoWhois_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
| summarize DomainCount=dcount(domain_name) by bin(TimeGenerated, 1h)
| where DomainCount > 5000
| project TimeGenerated, DomainCount

properties.displayName: WhoisFreaks - burst of newly registered domains

properties.description: Identifies high-confidence malware, phishing, and spam domains from WhoisFreaks threat feeds.
properties.query:
WhoisFreaksThreat_CL
| where toint(confidence) >= 80 or confidence =~ "high"
| summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) by domain, threat_type
| project TimeGenerated, domain, threat_type, confidence, first_seen, last_seen, is_parked, matched_pivots

properties.description: Identifies newly registered domains that are later observed in WhoisFreaks threat feeds.
properties.displayName: WhoisFreaks - newly registered domain seen in threat feed
properties.query:
let nrd = union WhoisFreaksNRD_CL, WhoisFreaksNRDNoWhois_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| distinct domain_name;
WhoisFreaksThreat_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| join kind=inner (nrd) on $left.domain == $right.domain_name
| summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) by domain, threat_type
| project TimeGenerated, domain, threat_type, confidence, domain_name

properties.displayName: WhoisFreaks - newly registered domain seen in threat feed

properties.description: Identifies threat-listed domains that are currently parked and may be used for staging.
properties.query:
WhoisFreaksThreat_CL
| where tostring(is_parked) =~ "true" or tostring(is_parked) == "1"
| summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) by domain
| project TimeGenerated, domain, threat_type, confidence, parked_reason, matched_pivots

connectorUiConfig.title: WhoisFreaks Threat & NRD Feeds (via Codeless Connector Framework)
connectorUiConfig.descriptionMarkdown: Ingest WhoisFreaks threat feeds and newly registered domain data into Microsoft Sentinel. Threat payload fields retain their API names. WHOIS NRD payload fields retain their API names. No-WHOIS NRD domains are stored in a dedicated table. Both NRD tables include an `nrd_type` column (`gtld` or `cctld`).

sampleQueries.query:
WhoisFreaksThreat_CL
| sort by TimeGenerated desc
| take 20

WhoisFreaksNRD_CL
| summarize count() by nrd_type
| sort by nrd_type asc

WhoisFreaksNRDNoWhois_CL
| summarize count() by nrd_type
| sort by nrd_type asc

properties.descriptionHtml:
Note: Please refer to the following before installing the solution:

• Review the solution Release Notes

• There may be known issues pertaining to this Solution, please refer to them before installing.

The WhoisFreaks solution for Microsoft Sentinel ingests commercial threat intelligence and newly registered domain (NRD) feeds through the Codeless Connector Framework into custom Log Analytics tables for hunting, detection, and investigation.

Underlying Microsoft Technologies used:

This solution depends on technologies that may be in Preview or incur additional ingestion or operational costs:

  1. Azure Monitor data collection rules

  2. Microsoft Sentinel

A WhoisFreaks API subscription and key entitled to the selected feeds are required.

Data Connectors: 1, Analytic Rules: 4
